=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-HtmlBlocks.md ===
# FEATURE: HTML Blocks

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Version | 20261027 V1 |
| Description | Recognize and preserve CommonMark HTML blocks. |
| Depends On | FEATURE-ParagraphsAndBreaks.md |
| Provides | HTML blocks |
| Consumes | paragraph and thematic break blocks |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose and behavior

The block parser recognizes HTML blocks after at most three spaces of indentation. It preserves their source lines as raw HTML without inline parsing. A block ends at the end of its containing block or document if its specific end condition is not reached.

Recognize the seven types defined in `sources/spec.txt`, “HTML blocks”:

1. A `pre`, `script`, `style`, or `textarea` opening begins a block ending on a line containing any of their closing tags, case-insensitively.
2. `<!--` begins a block ending on a line containing `-->`.
3. `<?` begins a block ending on a line containing `?>`.
4. `<!` followed by an ASCII letter begins a block ending on a line containing `>`.
5. `<![CDATA[` begins a block ending on a line containing `]]>`.
6. A specified block-level HTML tag begins a block ending before a blank line.
7. A complete open or closing tag on a line by itself begins a block ending before a blank line.

Types 1–6 can interrupt paragraphs; type 7 cannot. A start and end condition can occur on the same line, and the entire ending line belongs to the block. HTML inside an open block does not change its termination rule.

Expose `parse_html_block(lines, paragraph_open=False)` from `commonmark_parser.html_blocks`. It accepts a sequence of source lines and returns either `None` when no block starts or a pair `(consumed, raw)` containing the number of lines consumed and their unchanged concatenated text. The caller supplies only lines within the current container.

Cross-feature examples involving later inline constructs remain covered when those constructs are integrated.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC html-block-termination ===
Intent: A comment block retains its source through the line containing its end marker and leaves later lines unconsumed.

from commonmark_parser.html_blocks import parse_html_block

lines = ["<!-- start\n", "\n", "end --> trailing\n", "after\n"]
consumed, raw = parse_html_block(lines)
assert consumed == 3
assert raw == "".join(lines[:consumed])
=== END AC html-block-termination ===

=== AC html-block-paragraph-interruption ===
Intent: A complete non-block tag cannot interrupt a paragraph but can begin a type 7 HTML block outside one.

from commonmark_parser.html_blocks import parse_html_block

lines = ["<custom>\n", "content\n", "\n"]
assert parse_html_block(lines, paragraph_open=True) is None
consumed, raw = parse_html_block(lines, paragraph_open=False)
assert consumed == 2
assert raw == "".join(lines[:consumed])
=== END AC html-block-paragraph-interruption ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Do not modify the supplied specification or conformance assets.
- Preserve raw HTML rather than interpreting its contents as Markdown.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-ReferenceDefinitions.md ===
# FEATURE: Reference Definitions

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Version | 20261027 V1 |
| Description | Collect document-wide link reference definitions during block parsing. |
| Depends On | FEATURE-ParagraphsAndBreaks.md |
| Provides | reference definition map |
| Consumes | paragraph and thematic break blocks |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose and behavior

When a paragraph closes, parse consecutive definitions at its beginning and retain any remaining paragraph text. Definitions do not interrupt an existing paragraph. Apply the specification's label, destination, title, whitespace, indentation, and line-ending grammar. A definition can occur in a container and affects the entire document.

Normalize labels by Unicode case folding, trimming spaces, tabs, and line endings, and collapsing internal runs of those characters to one space. Preserve the first definition for each normalized label. Destinations and titles use the specified escape and character-reference rules.

Expose `collect_definitions(text, definitions)` from `commonmark_parser.references`. It updates the supplied document-wide dictionary in place and returns the unconsumed paragraph text. Dictionary values are `(destination, title)` pairs, with `None` for an omitted title. The caller invokes it when closing a paragraph in document order.

The later link and image stories exercise the reference-definition examples through the executable, including definitions inside containers and definitions appearing after uses.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC reference-first-definition ===
Intent: Matching labels share one document-wide entry and the earliest definition wins.

from commonmark_parser.references import collect_definitions

first = "/first"
second = "/second"
definitions = {}
collect_definitions("[Foo Bar]: " + first + "\n", definitions)
collect_definitions("[foo  bar]: " + second + "\n", definitions)
assert len(definitions) == 1
assert next(iter(definitions.values())) == (first, None)
=== END AC reference-first-definition ===

=== AC reference-remainder ===
Intent: Closing a paragraph removes its initial definition while retaining subsequent paragraph content.

from commonmark_parser.references import collect_definitions

destination = "/target"
remainder = "ordinary content\n"
definitions = {}
observed = collect_definitions("[label]: " + destination + "\n" + remainder, definitions)
assert observed == remainder
assert len(definitions) == 1
assert next(iter(definitions.values())) == (destination, None)
=== END AC reference-remainder ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Definitions are document-wide and the first matching definition takes precedence.
- Do not modify the supplied specification or conformance assets.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-BlockQuotes.md ===
# FEATURE: Block Quotes

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Version | 20261027 V1 |
| Description | Parse nested block quotes and their continuation lines. |
| Depends On | FEATURE-Headings.md, FEATURE-CodeBlocks.md, FEATURE-HtmlBlocks.md, FEATURE-ReferenceDefinitions.md |
| Provides | block quote containers |
| Consumes | paragraph and thematic break blocks, heading blocks, code blocks, HTML blocks, reference definition map |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose and behavior

A block quote marker is `>` preceded by at most three spaces and optionally followed by one space of indentation. Parse its contents as blocks, allowing nested quotes and all available leaf blocks. Match continuation markers through the open block tree before looking for new blocks. An omitted marker is permitted only on a paragraph continuation line; it cannot lazily continue a code block or introduce another block. Blank lines separate adjacent quotes unless included with quote markers. Quotes can interrupt paragraphs, and definitions inside them enter the document-wide reference map.

Expose `parse_block_quote(lines)` from `commonmark_parser.block_quotes`. It returns `None` if the first line does not start a quote; otherwise it returns `(consumed, content_lines)`, where `content_lines` are the source lines belonging to the quote after removing the outer marker and its optional following space. The block parser recursively parses those lines and preserves the distinction between marked and lazy continuation for block precedence.

Examples involving lists or later inline features are exercised after those capabilities are integrated.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC quote-markers ===
Intent: Consecutive marked lines form one quote and retain their contents for recursive block parsing.

from commonmark_parser.block_quotes import parse_block_quote

content = ["alpha\n", "beta\n"]
lines = ["> " + line for line in content] + ["\n"]
consumed, observed = parse_block_quote(lines)
assert consumed == len(content)
assert observed == content
=== END AC quote-markers ===

=== AC quote-lazy-continuation ===
Intent: An unmarked paragraph continuation remains inside its quote while a blank line terminates it.

from commonmark_parser.block_quotes import parse_block_quote

first = "alpha\n"
continuation = "beta\n"
lines = ["> " + first, continuation, "\n", "outside\n"]
consumed, observed = parse_block_quote(lines)
assert consumed == 2
assert observed == [first, continuation]
=== END AC quote-lazy-continuation ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Preserve the document-wide reference map across container boundaries.
- Do not modify the supplied specification or conformance assets.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Lists.md ===
# FEATURE: Lists

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Version | 20261027 V1 |
| Description | Parse CommonMark list items and list containers. |
| Depends On | FEATURE-BlockQuotes.md, FEATURE-ReferenceDefinitions.md, FEATURE-Headings.md, FEATURE-CodeBlocks.md, FEATURE-HtmlBlocks.md |
| Provides | list containers |
| Consumes | block quote containers, reference definition map, heading blocks, code blocks, HTML blocks |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose and behavior

Recognize bullet markers `-`, `+`, and `*`, and ordered markers of one to nine digits followed by `.` or `)`. A list groups consecutive items with the same bullet character or ordered delimiter. Its start number is that of its first ordered item.

Determine item content indentation from the marker width and following indentation, using the specification's special rules for an initial blank line and indented code. Match continuation indentation and allow lazy continuation only for paragraph continuation text. Parse nested blocks recursively, including quotes, lists, headings, code, HTML, and reference definitions. A thematic break takes precedence over a list marker. An empty item cannot interrupt a paragraph, and only an ordered item starting at one can interrupt one.

A list is loose when its items are separated by blank lines or an item directly contains blocks separated by a blank line; otherwise it is tight. Render paragraphs in loose items with paragraph tags and omit those tags for direct paragraphs in tight items.

Expose `parse_list_marker(line, paragraph_open=False)` from `commonmark_parser.lists`. It returns `None` for a line that cannot start an item; otherwise it returns a mapping with `kind`, `marker`, `start`, and `content_indent`. For bullets, `start` is `None`; for ordered markers it is the integer start value. `content_indent` is the number of indentation columns consumed before item content.

The complete List items and Lists sections and their inline interactions are exercised after all inline capabilities are integrated.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC list-marker ===
Intent: An ordered marker reports its start value and the indentation needed for its content.

from commonmark_parser.lists import parse_list_marker

number = 7
marker = f"{number}."
prefix = marker + "  "
result = parse_list_marker(prefix + "item\n")
assert result is not None
assert result["kind"] == "ordered"
assert result["marker"] == marker
assert result["start"] == number
assert result["content_indent"] == len(prefix)
=== END AC list-marker ===

=== AC list-paragraph-interruption ===
Intent: Only an ordered marker starting at one may interrupt a paragraph.

from commonmark_parser.lists import parse_list_marker

assert parse_list_marker("1. item\n", paragraph_open=True) is not None
assert parse_list_marker("2. item\n", paragraph_open=True) is None
assert parse_list_marker("-\n", paragraph_open=True) is None
=== END AC list-paragraph-interruption ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Follow the specification's block-tree continuation and precedence rules.
- Do not modify the supplied specification or conformance assets.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-EscapesAndEntities.md ===
# FEATURE: Escapes and Entities

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Version | 20261027 V1 |
| Description | Resolve CommonMark backslash escapes and character references in eligible contexts. |
| Depends On | FEATURE-Lists.md |
| Provides | inline escapes and character references |
| Consumes | list containers, reference definition map |

## Questions

- None.

## Purpose and behavior

After block structure and document-wide definitions are complete, parse inline content. A backslash escapes only ASCII punctuation; before other characters it remains literal. A backslash immediately before a line ending is a hard-break marker, handled by the line-break capability.

Recognize HTML5 named character references only with a terminating semicolon. Recognize decimal numeric references of one to seven digits and hexadecimal references of one to six digits, also requiring a semicolon. Replace invalid Unicode code points and U+0000 with U+FFFD according to the specification. References do not create structural Markdown delimiters. Neither escapes nor references are interpreted in code spans or code blocks; escapes do not apply inside autolinks or raw HTML.

Apply the same eligible escape and reference rules to destinations, titles, and fenced-code info strings. Preserve raw HTML attributes.

Expose `decode_escapes_and_entities(text)` from `commonmark_parser.inline`. It returns decoded text for an eligible plain-text context; the caller determines context and handles structural syntax before decoding.

The later integration story runs the complete Backslash escapes and Entity and numeric character references sections with links, images, code spans, autolinks, HTML, and line breaks available.

## Programmatic Acceptance

=== AC escaped-punctuation ===
Intent: A backslash before ASCII punctuation produces the punctuation supplied in the source.

from commonmark_parser.inline import decode_escapes_and_entities

punctuation = "*"
source = "\\" + punctuation
assert decode_escapes_and_entities(source) == punctuation
=== END AC escaped-punctuation ===

=== AC unescaped-character ===
Intent: A backslash before a non-punctuation character remains literal.

from commonmark_parser.inline import decode_escapes_and_entities

source = "\\a"
assert decode_escapes_and_entities(source) == source
=== END AC unescaped-character ===

=== AC numeric-reference ===
Intent: A valid numeric character reference resolves to the character represented by its supplied code point.

from commonmark_parser.inline import decode_escapes_and_entities

codepoint = 65
source = f"&#{codepoint};"
assert decode_escapes_and_entities(source) == chr(codepoint)
=== END AC numeric-reference ===

## User Acceptance

- None.

## Guardrails

- Parse blocks and collect reference definitions before parsing inlines.
- Do not use a public Markdown implementation or modify the supplied conformance assets.
=== END ARTIFACT ===
